solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 19 across to 20); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: She was wise to sunbathe naked — just a bit

indicators.note: just a bit says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A wise woman is advised to sunbathe with only a little nudity.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek goddess of wisdom is the woman described as being wise.

clue.text: Nothing missing, being quite astute

definitions.meaning: mentally sharp and alert, not at all slow-witted

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes both something complete and a person with full mental faculties.

clue.text: Life in the future, present and past

parts.note: being present means being here
past as in half past, meaning after

explanation.surface: A tense-by-tense description of life: future, present and past.
explanation.walkthrough: The three tenses look like a grammar list, but only 'the future' belongs to the definition; 'present' and 'past' build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The afterlife is the existence believed to follow death, a life still to come.

clue.text: Heads of Nato offer everyone leave for Christmas

indicators.note: heads of the following words means take the first letter of each one

explanation.surface: Military alliance leaders give all their staff time off over the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a traditional word for Christmas, as in carols.

clue.text: What lazybones might say, as a pagan

parts.note: a lazy person putting off a job might say 'I do it later', here I DO
the second half of the idler's excuse is LATER

explanation.surface: A lazy person's excuse is likened to the words of a heathen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I do later' as a procrastinator's promise; run together, it spells a worshipper of idols.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships images or false gods, which is what a pagan was taken to do.

clue.text: Army sniper and (reversed) how he met his match!

parts.note: a marksman beaten by a better one was shot dead, and with the two words turned round this gives the first word
the other word of the turned-round phrase about his fate

explanation.surface: A soldier marksman and, turned round, the way he finally lost to a better shot.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed word swaps the order of the two words of his fate, not their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead shot is an unerringly accurate marksman, like a skilled army sniper.

clue.text: Pine handcart discovered in ancient burial site

parts.note: to pine for something is to long for it
a barrow is a small cart pushed by hand

explanation.surface: Wooden pushcart unearthed in an archaeological dig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the timber of the cart, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: A long barrow is an elongated prehistoric earth mound covering graves, found across Britain.

clue.text: Thatcher saw him as the competition

definitions.text: Thatcher saw him as the competition

parts.words: Thatcher saw him as the competition
parts.note: a roof thatcher's rival trade is the person who covers roofs with slates or tiles

explanation.walkthrough: The capital T suggests Margaret Thatcher and political rivals, but this is a thatcher of roofs.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer laying tiles competes with a thatcher for the same roofing work.

clue.text: Sailor's rocket

definitions.meaning: a non-commissioned seaman in the navy, read as 'sailor is'
a rocket is a severe telling-off

explanation.definitionFit: A rating is a naval rank-and-file sailor, and also a sharp scolding, a rocket in British slang.

clue.text: Euros, oddly, support American addicts

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below the other
oddly means take the first, third and fifth letters of the word

explanation.surface: European money props up drug-dependent Americans.
explanation.definitionFit: Users is a common term for people who take drugs habitually.

clue.text: The generosity shown by great saints

parts.note: great means big, large
S is the abbreviation for saint, SS for saints

explanation.surface: Saints are praised for their open-handed kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: Largess is generous giving of money or gifts, open-handed generosity.

clue.text: A tunnel shaped like a small ring

indicators.note: shaped means the letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A passageway built in a circular form.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulet is a little ring, especially a ringed moulding on a column or a heraldic charge.

clue.text: Wreck of a car in pile-up

definitions.meaning: an old dilapidated vehicle, a banger
to pile up, to stack things in a mound

explanation.definitionFit: A heap is slang for a broken-down car, and as a verb means to pile up.

clue.text: Persevere, without lawyers, to expose media mogul

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the lawyers sit inside the other phrase

parts.note: to press on is to keep going despite difficulty
the bar is the body of barristers

explanation.surface: Keep going without legal help to unmask a newspaper tycoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it is the old sense of outside, so the lawyers end up enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: A press baron is a powerful newspaper owner, a mogul of the print media.

clue.text: Two-thirds gin mixed with lemonade in ideal proportions

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters are stirred into a new order
two of its three letters are kept, here the outer pair of the word

explanation.surface: A cocktail recipe: a measure of gin topped up with lemonade.
explanation.walkthrough: Two-thirds of 'gin' gives GN, mixed with LEMONADE.
explanation.definitionFit: The golden mean is the ratio of ideal proportion, also the principle of moderation between extremes.

clue.text: No sailor returned without one share

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, wrapping round the single letter
returned means the pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a tar is a sailor
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: No seaman came back without getting his allotted portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reads the phrase backwards as RATON, and 'without' wraps that round the numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed allotted portion, one person's allowance.

clue.text: Third-rate fight once appreciated by the penniless

parts.note: something third-rate is of poor quality
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A shoddy boxing bout that only the destitute enjoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor box was a church collection box whose takings went to needy people.

clue.text: They're supposed to attract rich and poor, for instance

definitions.meaning: the saying is that unlike things draw together
a pair of contrasting words with contrary meanings

explanation.definitionFit: Opposites attract, as the proverb says, and contrary pairs such as rich and poor are antonyms.

clue.text: Most petrified girl imprisoned by crazy Tess

indicators.note: imprisoned by means the girl's name is held inside the other letters
crazy means the letters of the name are scrambled

parts.note: Toni is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A frightened young woman is held captive by a mad woman called Tess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' rearranges the name into SEST, and 'imprisoned by' sets the girl's name inside after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrified means turned to stone, so the most petrified thing is the most stony.

clue.text: Some phone numbers are a hidden message

parts.note: a code is a concealed message

explanation.surface: Certain telephone numbers conceal a secret communication.
explanation.definitionFit: An area code is the dialling prefix of phone numbers in one region.

clue.text: Heartless cashier alters moneys paid in

indicators.note: heartless means the middle is removed, keeping just the first and last letters

parts.note: to edit is to alter a text

explanation.surface: An unfeeling bank teller tampers with deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: Credits are sums entered to an account, money paid into it.

clue.text: Stop perspiration showing inside expensive hat

indicators.note: showing inside says the answer is visible within the run of letters of those words

explanation.surface: Keep sweat from marking the lining of a pricey hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A topper is a top hat, a tall and costly formal silk hat.

clue.text: Assist in motion or its opposite [i.e. of motion]

indicators.note: in motion means the letters are moving into a new order

explanation.surface: Help something moving, or else its stillness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to motion, so the definition is the opposite of motion.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of inactivity or equilibrium, the absence of motion.

clue.text: Puzzle [is what] an axeman would leave behind

definitions.meaning: the base of a tree trunk left after felling

explanation.definitionFit: To stump is to baffle; a stump is the remnant a woodcutter leaves of a felled tree.

clue.text: Cause great confusion with identical speeds at sea?

parts.note: two ships drawing level in knots, nautical miles per hour, are in a tie

explanation.surface: Muddle everyone with ships going at the same speed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as a dead heat (a tie) measured in knots, the unit of speed at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie someone in knots is an idiom for confusing or flustering them badly.

clue.text: Extra large is said to be better

indicators.note: is said means the letters are spoken aloud to give the word

parts.note: XL is the clothing size for extra large

explanation.surface: A bigger size is claimed to be superior.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken as letters, X L sounds like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstanding, superior to others.

clue.text: A part of Thailand formerly located here

definitions.text: A part of Thailand formerly located here

indicators.note: part of means only some of the old name is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Siam was the old name of Thailand

explanation.surface: A clue about where the old kingdom of Thailand lay on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' plus most of SIAM gives the continent where Siam lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand, once Siam, is located in this continent.

clue.text: A beautiful fairy spells endless danger

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: peril means danger

explanation.surface: A lovely sprite casts magic that brings unending peril.
explanation.definitionFit: In Persian myth a peri is a beautiful fairy-like spirit.

clue.text: Hide in middle of desert island

indicators.note: middle of means take the central letters of the word

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island

explanation.surface: Conceal yourself on a deserted island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a verb for abandoning, but only its middle letters SE are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete is to conceal something somewhere hidden.

clue.text: Ring-master to retrain as a conductor

indicators.note: to retrain means the letters are retaught into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A circus ringmaster retrains to lead an orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring-master' looks like one word but splits: Ring gives O, and 'to retrain' rearranges MASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestro is a title for a distinguished orchestral conductor.

clue.text: Feature of seawater that's 51, within reason

indicators.note: within means the number is placed inside the other word

parts.note: sanity is soundness of mind, reason
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A trait of the sea that is fifty-one, within reasonable limits.
explanation.walkthrough: Roman numerals are a crossword staple: a number in a clue often stands for its numeral letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Salinity is saltiness, a defining property of seawater.

clue.text: Paper used to make up lies?

definitions.meaning: thin soft paper for wiping or wrapping
a whole set of untruths is called a web or fabric of lies

explanation.definitionFit: Tissue is thin paper, and a tissue of lies is a web of falsehoods.
